title: Checkpoint: What Psychology Is
objective: After this level you can explain how psychology grew from philosophy into a science that tests ideas about the mind.
summary: Questions about the mind were philosophy until the 1800s. Then labs, rival schools and new methods turned psychology into a science that tests its ideas.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale: from arguing about the mind to testing it.
cards.body: Philosophers have puzzled over the mind since ancient Greece. Psychology's twist was to start checking the answers. First, where the questions came from; then the whole chapter on one timeline.

cards.headline: From armchair to laboratory
cards.body: Attempts to understand the mind go back at least to Greek philosophers such as Plato and Aristotle. From then on, the study of mind stayed part of philosophy until the nineteenth century, when experimental psychology developed. By the late 1800s psychology was accepted as its own academic discipline, and Wilhelm Wundt in Germany and William James in the United States are generally credited as its founders.

cards.headline: Psychology's first century, in five moves

events.label: Wundt opens the first psychology lab, in Leipzig
Watson launches behaviorism: study only what you can observe
Chomsky argues behaviorism can't explain language
Neisser publishes the textbook Cognitive Psychology

cards.headline: Tested ideas win
cards.body: Look at what lasted. Freud's specific theories mostly failed their tests, while his broad idea of an unconscious mind found support. Case studies still offer rich detail but are hard to generalize. The pattern across the chapter is the point: psychology keeps what survives testing.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: How psychology grew from philosophy's questions into a science that measures the mind.
Why behaviorists set the mind aside, and how the cognitive revolution brought it back.
What case studies, observation, surveys and twin studies can and can't show about people.
Why research on people now needs informed consent and approval from an ethics board.

questions.prompt: Until the nineteenth century, which field held the study of the mind?

options.label: Medicine
options.rationale: Medicine trained Wundt and Freud, but the study of mind belonged to philosophy.

options.label: Linguistics
options.rationale: Linguistics joined much later, in the cognitive revolution.

options.label: Computer science
options.rationale: Computers arrived in the twentieth century.

questions.explanation: From Plato and Aristotle until the nineteenth century, the study of mind was part of philosophy.

questions.prompt: Put these events in the order they happened, from earliest to latest.
items: Wundt opens the first psychology lab
questions.explanation: Wundt opened the first psychology lab in 1879, Watson launched behaviorism in 1913, and Neisser published Cognitive Psychology in 1967.

questions.prompt: Which of Freud's ideas has support from later research?

options.label: His stages of childhood development
options.rationale: Most of his specific claims like these found no support.

options.label: That much of mental life is unconscious
That interpretations are enough proof
options.rationale: That is why his specific claims failed.

options.label: That all behavior depends only on rewards
options.rationale: That was the behaviorist view, not Freud's.

questions.explanation: A large body of research supports Freud's broad idea that much of mental life happens outside awareness.

questions.prompt: Why are case studies hard to generalize from?

options.label: They collect too little detail
options.rationale: They collect more detail than any other single method.

options.label: They always pool answers from thousands of people
options.rationale: A case study focuses on one person or just a few.

options.label: They often study people with rare characteristics
They are banned by ethics boards
options.rationale: Case studies are allowed with consent.

questions.explanation: Case studies often focus on unusual people, so their findings may not apply to most others.

questions.prompt: Chomsky challenged behaviorism in 1959 by reviewing _____ book.
questions.explanation: Chomsky's 1959 review of Skinner's book on verbal behavior argued behaviorism couldn't explain language learning.
